summary.intent: Complete Phase 23 (Rust SDK extraction) gap closure, run a security review on the extracted crates, add unit test coverage to address Codecov feedback, and get PR #352 merged.
summary.outcome: Phase 23 gap closure was completed (plan 23-08), security review identified and fixed 2 HIGH findings (Ed25519 zeroization + ed25519-dalek zeroize feature), 163 new unit tests were added across 3 crates, CI failures were fixed (Windows cargo check + cross-language parity), and PR review comments were addressed — though the final commit was blocked by 1Password SSH signing.

repo: The workspace [patch.crates-io] for vendored fuser causes Cargo to resolve and compile the crate on ALL platforms even when it's optional and feature-gated — fix requires [target.'cfg(unix)'.dependencies] in all Cargo.toml files that reference it
ed25519-dalek requires the 'zeroize' feature flag to be explicitly enabled in workspace Cargo.toml for SigningKey to zero on drop — it does NOT happen automatically
KeyState and CipherBoxFS key fields already use Zeroizing<Vec<u8>> and clear on logout/unmount — the existing zeroization architecture is sound
The desktop app uses AES-CTR mode for IPFS content (not GCM) and relies on IPFS CID for integrity rather than client-side MAC verification — a known design tradeoff
generate_ed25519_keypair callers in fuse/write_ops.rs were already wrapping the return value in redundant Zeroizing::new() — changing the return type to Zeroizing<Vec<u8>> allowed simplification
CI runs cargo llvm-cov --workspace on Linux for Rust coverage reporting to Codecov
The five Rust crates (crypto, core, fuse, sdk, api-client) had almost no unit tests before this session — only 5 cross-language tests in crypto and 11 vault_blob tests in core
registry.rs had a copy-paste bug where device_entry.app_version was being set to device_info.device_id instead of device_info.app_version

code.finding: generate_ed25519_keypair returned bare Vec<u8> for private key — changed to Zeroizing<Vec<u8>> to prevent key material lingering in freed memory
Caller was wrapping generate_ed25519_keypair result in redundant Zeroizing::new() — simplified after return type change
ipns_private_key.try_into() consuming Zeroizing<Vec<u8>> required Vec::from() unwrap before TryInto<[u8; 32]>
Same try_into() issue on Windows path — Zeroizing<Vec<u8>> doesn't implement TryInto<[u8; 32]> directly
fetch_and_populate_folder and resolve_file_pointers_blocking were dead code — no callers outside themselves in both Unix and Windows paths
Copy-paste bug: app_version field set to device_info.device_id instead of pre-saved app_version — device_info was partially moved so the field was consumed
Vendored fuser build.rs called unimplemented!() on non-Linux platforms without libfuse — needed early return for Windows, but this alone was insufficient since Rust source still compiled
fuser dependency moved from top-level optional to [target.'cfg(unix)'.dependencies] optional to prevent Cargo from resolving it on Windows
Same fuser gating fix needed here — both Cargo.tomls reference fuser and both needed the target cfg gate
pnpm/action-setup@v4 in cross-language parity job was missing 'version: 10' — other jobs in the same workflow had it

workflow: When an agent disconnects mid-execution, spot-check via git log before retrying — both task commits may already exist and only bookkeeping (SUMMARY.md, STATE.md, ROADMAP.md) remains

Cargo [patch.crates-io] applies workspace-wide and cannot be conditionally activated by cfg — the only way to prevent platform-specific compilation is to gate the dependency itself under [target.'cfg(...)'.dependencies]
Moving optional deps from top-level to target-specific sections in Cargo.toml is backward compatible — features still work on the target platform
The classifyHandoffIfNeeded error is a Claude Code runtime bug that fires after tool calls complete — treat as success if spot-checks pass (SUMMARY.md exists, commits present)
1Password SSH signing is flaky and sometimes requires multiple retries — the agent should retry 2-3 times before giving up and asking the user

friction: 1Password SSH agent signing failures required multiple retries and ultimately blocked the final commit of the PR review fixes
Initial gsd-executor agent disconnected mid-execution (API ConnectionRefused) requiring manual resume and bookkeeping
Windows cargo check fix required two iterations — fixing the build.rs was insufficient because the Rust source still compiled; needed to move the dependency under cfg(unix) target
gh CLI run/job log fetching was unreliable — multiple bash commands needed to extract actual error lines from CI output
Cargo [patch.crates-io] behavior (resolving patched crates even when optional and feature-gated) is non-obvious and caused the Windows build failure
open_items: AES-CTR client-side integrity verification gap — client doesn't verify IPFS CID after fetching bytes, relying on relay trustworthiness; deferred from security review
file_ipns_private_key in write_ops.rs uses ed25519_dalek SigningKey directly (not via generate_ed25519_keypair) and returns plain Vec<u8> — not addressed in this session
Security review generated ~30 test case suggestions for attack scenarios (replay, timing, key confusion) that were not implemented — only positive/negative/edge cases added
fuse crate still has pre-existing dead code warnings from vendored fuser crate (not our code) — not cleaned up
The security review report (.planning/security/REVIEW-2026-03-24-phase23.md) noted 4 MEDIUM and 5 LOW findings that were not fixed in this session
